MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  February 3, 2025

Chair Greenidge called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll
call were Chair Greenidge, Vice Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Pena, Commissioner
Apodaca Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Rosoff, Commissioner Brizuela and
Commissioner Fernandez-Silva, absent Commissioner Hoskins. Also present were
Richard Newton, Interim Director, Public Safety Manager Rita Ruiz, Interim OEM
Manager Jazmine Salas and Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Fernandez-Silva motioned for the approval of minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on February 3, 2025. Commissioner Dr.
Rodriguez seconded the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES: Chair Greenidge, Vice Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Apodaca,
  Commissioner Pena, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner
  Rosoff, Commissioner Brizuela
NOES: None
ABSENT: Commissioner Hoskins
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

Mrs. Lomas called for the reorganization of Chair and Vice Chair. Commissioner Rosoff
nominated Vice Chair LeGaspi for the position of Chair.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES: Commissioner Greenidge, Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Apodaca,
  Commissioner Pena, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner
  Rosoff, Commissioner Brizuela
NOES: None
ABSENT: Commissioner Hoskins
ABSTAIN: None

Mrs. Lomas asked for the nomination for Vice Chair. Commissioner Apodaca nominated
Commissioner Rosoff for the position of Vice Chair. Chair LeGaspi second the motion.
Mrs. Lomas recorded the motion of approval.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:
 AYES: Commissioner Greenidge, Chair Legaspi, Commissioner Apodaca,
  Commissioner Pena, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Vice Chair Rosoff,
  Commissioner Brizuela
NOES: None
ABSENT: Commissioner Hoskins
ABSTAIN: None

Mr. Newton gave his congratulations to the new Chair and Vice Chair.

Mrs. Lomas advised that Norwalk Public Safety Manager Rita Ruiz will be providing a
report on Street Takeovers. Rita Ruiz advised of recent concerns regarding street
takeovers at the intersection of Rosecrans and Pioneer. Concerns have been reported by
our residents, businesses and community members. An overnight detail was
implemented and aimed at enhancing safety and preventing further gatherings. Mrs. Ruiz
advised that the overnight parking detail consists of the deployment of 1 Public Safety
Sergeant, 2 Public Safety Officers, 1 Dispatcher from 10:00 p.m.- 6:00 a.m. The shift had
later changed to 10:00 p.m.-3:00 a.m. Friday -Saturday. Camera trailers, the MPC/ RV
were deployed near the intersection. Mrs. Ruiz reported that the department has been
successful in deterring a few events/gatherings and has provided a safer environment for
everyone. A few motorists contacted officers inquiring about the officer’s presence in the
area. Some of the questions were how long they would be out there, what we are doing
and some happy to see us addressing street takeovers. Overall, we did notice a decrease
in activity.

Mr. Newton advised that the City Council adopted two Norwalk Municipal Code in 2022 for
Speeding contest or Exhibition of Speed and Spector during presentation of unlawful
speed contest or unlawful exhibition of speed. This will allow for the enforcement of
administrative fines Offenses and fees 1st $2,000.00, 2nd $3,000.00 and 3rd $5,000.00.
There are also new Legislation in 2025; Assembly Bills 1978, 2186,2807 and 3035 that
allow for seize of vehicle, impounding vehicles for up to 30 days, standardizes existing
language to clarify that a vehicle sideshow is also known as a “Street Takeover” and
permits law enforcement to impound vehicles suspected of involvement of street takeover
or racing on highways or parking lots with a warrant or judge’s order, similar to current
evading police laws.

Mr. Newton stated that the collaborative efforts of Public Safety along with LASD, Public
services and Engineering to implement the following: Community Outreach, Leveraging
Technology, High Visibility Patrols and Engineering. We will be working with the
community and identify those responsible for the activity. Engineering is considering
Roadway design and modification to curtail activity. LASD/Public Safety are using
Enforcement and Education and are implementing the campaign, “See Something Say
Something” via social media and publications. Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez questioned
how we would be educating the public and Mr. Newton advised that we will be posting on
our social media accounts and publications. Commissioner Brizuela requested
clarification on whether fees would be applied to first-time offenders. Mr. Newton
confirmed that the city intends to fully enforce these fees as a deterrent to those engaging
in the activity. Chair R. LeGaspi brought attention to the street takeover incident on
January 11, 2025, specifically regarding the vehicle that was set on fire. Additionally, he
inquired about Sheriff’s response or lack thereof to such incidents. Mr. Newton
 emphasized the importance of ensuring the safety of both deputies and officers and
mentioned the presence of a dedicated task force to address these situations.
.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Lomas went over the February 2025 calendar.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez commented on Bob White Park parking concerns related to
Costco shopper parking in the parking lot. Mr. Newton mentioned that he would be
available after the meeting to discuss it.

Commissioner Greenridge commented on illegal dumping in front of her home.
Mentioning that she was advised to call Quadrant Officer Jimmy Gomez and contact
Public Safety. Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez advised that she could share instructions on
how to submit complaints and work orders online through the city website.

Commissioner Fernandez-Silva commented and would like to take Public Safety staff
regarding a call for service that he called in regarding a person that was loitering in his
area.

Chair Legaspi commented on the Homeless Count advising of the change in data and
requested more information for volunteer and he was advised to contact the Social
Services office.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:35PM.
 _______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
